findings.title: Excellence as measured making
findings.claim: The focus’s universal good-making can be read as skilled, measured production that brings even clay into a balanced human form.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries good action in أَحْسَنَ, measurement and boundary-setting in خَلَقَهُ/خَلْقَ, balanced form in the repeated creation root, and literal clay in طِين. Wider passages say that every thing is created according to measure, that human creation is followed by proportioning, and that the human is made in the best form. Iblis’s later fire-versus-clay contrast supplies the independent material-status trigger: clay can be treated as lowly while the focus’s measured making gives it fitting form.
findings.reader_payoff: A humble material origin and excellent formation become parts of one act: the material’s rank does not determine the quality of the resulting form.
findings.containment: Clay remains the literal material in 32:7, and the low-status comparison belongs to Iblis’s speech, not to the focus as an endorsed judgment. The wider passages clarify measure and form without replacing the focus’s plain creation claim.

epistemic.reason: The published finding is trusted and its focus branches are registered; wider connection rows supply exact Arabic but not target morphology. The claim about clay’s lower rank is therefore attributed to the counter-voice and the extension remains qualified.
